newsitem.title: UK: Britain worried about West Bank violence.
newsitem.headline: Britain worried about West Bank violence.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it was worried about renewed violence in the West Bank and reiterated that it considered all Jewish settlements in the occupied territories illegal.
"We are deeply concerned by reports of violence returning to the West Bank," said a foreign office spokesman.
He said the death of a Palestinian during demonstrations against Israeli settlements reinforced "the urgency of restoring momentum to the Palestinian track of the Peace Process".
Israeli troops shot dead a Palestinian man and wounded 11 in the West Bank village of Deir Kidis near Ramallah during an Arab protest against land confiscations, witnesses said on Sunday.
The shooting occurred near where Palestinians say Israelis confiscated 1,250 acres (500 hectares) for a Jewish settlement.
An army spokesman said the incident was under investigation.
Israel still occupies much of the West Bank despite handing over most cities there to Palestinian self-rule under peace deals with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).
The PLO insists the confiscations violate interim peace deals but Israel maintains the issue of settlements is only to be resolved in future final-status talks.
During a visit to the west bank town of Hebron last week, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said Britain believed all Jewish settlements in the occupied territories were illegal.
Hebron is still occupied by Israeli troops months after the deadline for their redeployment.
"As the Foreign Secretary emphasised during his visit to Hebron... settlements are illegal and an obstacle to peace," the foreign office spokesman said on Monday.
"Expansion of settlements erodes trust, which needs to be restored for a serious start to...final status negotiations."
Rifkind visited Israel and the West Bank for talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian president Yasser Arafat.
